problem: The text says order: 2 'also moves it for screen readers and Tab order'. That is false. order changes only the visual order; the accessibility tree and keyboard Tab sequence still follow the HTML source. The next sentence and the Q7 answer both state the correct rule, so the chapter contradicts itself.
fix: order: 2 moves an item later on the screen without touching the HTML. Screen readers and Tab order still follow the HTML source, so the visual and spoken sequences differ. Never use it to reorder content that has a meaningful sequence.

where: Exam traps, fourth bullet (z-index / stacking contexts)
problem: The trap says a child cannot paint above 'a sibling of its parent that has a lower stacking context'. A sibling with a lower stacking context is painted below, so the child would paint above it. The real limit is a sibling of the parent that paints above the parent, i.e. a sibling with a higher z-index or a later stacking context. As written the rule says the opposite of what happens.
fix: A child is trapped inside its parent's stacking context. A z-index: 9999 child still paints below any element outside that context that stacks above the parent, such as a sibling of the parent with a higher z-index.

where: Exam traps, fourth bullet, first clause
problem: 'z-index does nothing on a static-positioned box' clashes with Section 1, which correctly says z-index also works on flex and grid items. A static flex item does respond to z-index.
fix: z-index is ignored on an ordinary static box; it applies to positioned boxes and to flex and grid items.

problem: srcset is described as picking 'by pixel density' only. With width descriptors the browser also needs the sizes attribute and picks by the layout width the image will occupy, which is the usual responsive case.
fix: srcset lists several files with width descriptors plus a sizes attribute; the browser picks the file whose width suits the space the image will occupy and the screen's pixel density.

problem: minmax(150px, 1fr) is said to set 'a floor and a ceiling'. The 1fr maximum is flexible, not a ceiling; the track can still grow past it when the container is wide.
fix: minmax(150px, 1fr) sets a floor of 150 px and lets the track grow freely above it, sharing the leftover space with the other fr tracks.
